title: Simple Machines
description: Try a lever, a pulley, and a ramp, and see how each one trades a longer move for a smaller effort.
prerequisites: A push can lift a crate
learningObjectives: Explain how a lever, a pulley, or a ramp trades a longer distance for a smaller effort.
Choose a machine that lifts a heavy crate with a smaller push.

params.description: Which simple machine the lesson asks the child to try first.

events.name: machine_selected
events.description: The child chose a lever, a pulley, or a ramp.

events.name: advantage_compared
events.description: The child compared the machine's push with lifting the crate straight up.

tutorGuide.intro: A simple machine spreads one lift over a longer path, so the push gets smaller. Try a lever, a pulley, and a ramp on the same crate.
steps: Find the fulcrum, the rope, or the slope.
Read the push and the advantage.
observationPrompts: Which part moves farther, your hand or the crate?
What happens to the push when the path gets longer?

misconceptions.response: The crate still rises. You push less hard because you push farther.

misconceptions.belief: A ramp is not a machine.
misconceptions.response: A ramp is an inclined plane. A longer slope means a smaller push.

hints: Tap one of the three machines.
Look at the number called advantage.
A bigger advantage means a smaller push and a longer path.

successCriteria.description: Chose a machine and compared its advantage with a straight lift.

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: Three machines lift one crate. A lever, a pulley, and a ramp each make the push smaller and the distance longer.
